newsitem.title: USA: Great Western says claim lacks factual basis.
newsitem.headline: Great Western says claim lacks factual basis.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp said Sunday the claim made by H.F. Ahmanson and Co on Friday that Great Western and Washington Mutual Savings Bank will not be able to use pooling-of-interests accounting for their proposed merger "has no factual basis whatsoever."
The company, which has a definitive agreement to merge with Washington Mutual, called Ahmanson's charge baseless.

"Ahmanson's latest attack on Great Western's proposed business combination with Washington Mutual Inc is baseless both as an accounting matter and as to any claim of lack of candor by Great Western's board of directors," the company said.
Ahmanson filed on Friday a proposed amendment to its lawsuit against Great Western that claimed Great Western took certain actions that may preclude a pooling transaction.

Great Western said it and Washington Mutual were fully aware of the requirements for pooling-of-interests accounting treatment and have been advised by their accounting firms that pooling-of-interests accounting is "appropriate" for the proposed merger.

Ahmanson recently raised its hostile stock exchange offer to between 1.10 and 1.20 Ahmanson shares for each Great Western share. Washington Mutual reached a definitive agreement with Great Western on March 6 to swap 0.9 of its shares for each Great Western share.
